source_name: Magyar Posta supplier bidding via SAP Ariba Sourcing
why_relevant: Posta's notices state that detailed tender conditions and bid submission run through SAP Ariba Sourcing with mandatory supplier registration — meaning the substantive documentation is behind a supplier login, which caps what open collection can see and is itself an intelligence fact about access.

source_name: MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank – Gazdálkodási adatok (procurement plan, procedures, contracts)
why_relevant: MFB's statutory disclosure section explicitly covers annual statistical summaries, procurement plans, procurement procedures, centralised procurement contracts and bid-evaluation summaries — the primary window on the development bank as a buyer (incl. the MFB Pont intermediary-network tenders).

source_name: EXIM (Eximbank / MEHIB) – Közbeszerzési információk
why_relevant: Dedicated procurement-information page in EXIM's általános közzétételi lista, carrying the procurement plan and pointers to the Közbeszerzési Adatbázis / EKR entries for the export-import bank and export credit insurer.

source_name: EXIM – Az Eximbank és a MEHIB gazdálkodásával összefüggő szerződések
why_relevant: Contract register (5 MFt+ / national-threshold contracts): counterparty, subject, value and amendments. This is where an awarded payments/IT supplier actually becomes visible even when the tender itself was low-profile.

source_name: Diákhitel Központ – Közbeszerzésekkel kapcsolatos közzétételek
why_relevant: Student Loan Centre (MFB-owned) publishes its procurement plan and its modifications; observed procurements include network equipment, mobile telecom and complex communications — i.e. the IT/service layer of a state lender.

source_name: Diákhitel Központ – Közbeszerzési eljárásban megjelent hirdetmények
why_relevant: The notice-level companion page: individual contract notices and award notices per procedure, giving vendor names and values directly.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – Közérdekű adatok
why_relevant: The Hungarian CSD (MNB-group) publishes public-interest data incl. contract and procurement-type disclosures; KELER buys settlement/depository IT, connectivity and security services directly relevant to post-trade payments infrastructure.

source_name: KELER KSZF Zrt. – Közérdekű adatok
why_relevant: The central counterparty's separate disclosure page; distinct legal entity from KELER Zrt., so it procures separately (clearing systems, risk/collateral IT).

source_name: GIRO Zrt. – corporate site (BKR / AFR operator, MNB-owned)
why_relevant: Operator of the interbank clearing system (BKR) and the instant payment system (AFR), 100% MNB-owned. No public tender page was found, but its business rules, news and service launches (e.g. GIROFix) plus its Nets A/S supplier selection are the best open proxy for its vendor pipeline.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer, hirdetmények (notice search)
why_relevant: The national e-procurement platform where all these buyers' notices are filed and where bids are submitted. Filtering by ajánlatkérő (MNB, Kincstár, Posta, MFB, EXIM, Diákhitel, KELER, GIRO) is the single highest-yield systematic feed for this cell.

source_name: EKR – Ajánlatkérő nyilvántartás (register of contracting authorities)
why_relevant: Authoritative list of registered contracting authorities — the way to confirm which of MNB, Kincstár, MFB, EXIM, Posta, KELER, GIRO, Diákhitel are formally ajánlatkérő and under which regime (classic vs utility), and to snowball to further state-influenced financial buyers we have not named.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Közbeszerzési Értesítő / Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA)
why_relevant: The official gazette and central database of Hungarian procurement notices and contracts. Individual notices for MFB, Posta and MNB were reachable here with stable per-notice URLs, making it a durable retrieval and backfill layer behind EKR.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ S), Hungarian financial-sector buyers
source_subtype: supranational tender gazette / open data API
why_relevant: Above-threshold notices from these buyers are published in the EU OJ S (e.g. the MFB Pontok network expansion notice 2016/S 219-399038). TED gives structured, machine-readable, CPV-coded coverage in EN and HU and is linked from MNB's own procurement page.

source_name: eGov Hírlevél – Közbeszerzési Értesítő digest (digitális kormányzati közbeszerzések tag)
why_relevant: Editorially curated periodic digest of IT/digital-government notices selected from the Közbeszerzési Értesítő — a pre-filtered, low-effort way to catch relevant state-sector IT and payments tenders and to learn the vocabulary buyers use.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer, public eljárástár (procedure browser)
why_relevant: The single platform where Hungarian contracting authorities actually run procedures; since mid-2024 the public procedure browser supports structured search by CPV, subject and place of performance, and offers an e-mail notice-watch service. Primary feed for live banking/POS/e-payment tenders by non-financial public buyers.

source_name: CoRe – Közbeszerzési Hatóság szerződésnyilvántartó (contract registry) public search
why_relevant: Mandatory registry of concluded public procurement contracts, modifications and performance data since 2018. Gives the award side: which bank won which municipality/hospital account or acquiring contract, value, duration, modifications — i.e. contract renewal windows.

source_name: Napitender / InnoTender tender-monitoring services
why_relevant: Secondary aggregators/consultancies; their public blog and category pages sometimes surface individual notices and buyer names that help snowball the actor map, even without subscribing.

source_name: openprocurements.com – Hungarian buyer profiles (hu.openprocurements.com)
why_relevant: Third-party mirror organised by BUYER, which is the axis this cell needs (per-hospital, per-university, per-municipality procurement history). Handy for quickly enumerating a buyer's past financial-services contracts.

source_name: BKK Budapesti Közlekedési Központ – hírek / e-jegy (Pay&GO) programme communications
why_relevant: BKK is the single largest payments-acceptance buyer in this cell. Its news feed announced the Pay&GO contactless rollout to all metro lines (April 2026) and the Budapest e-ticket concept approved by the Metropolitan Assembly in Feb 2026 authorising BKK to launch the procurement — an early-warning signal months ahead of the notice.

source_name: MÁV-csoport közbeszerzések (MÁV Szolgáltató Központ Zrt.)
why_relevant: Central procurement page of the national railway group; buys ticket vending machines with payment capability (JKA automata), their L3 support/maintenance, and card acceptance for ticketing — a recurring payments-hardware and acquiring demand pool.

source_name: BKV Zrt. közérdekű adatok / közbeszerzési terv és beszerzések
why_relevant: BKV publishes its annual közbeszerzési terv (procurement plan) and Kbt.-mandated data, and points to EKR and CoRe for its procedures/contracts. The forward-looking plan is the cheapest early indicator of upcoming payment/ticketing and banking-service purchases.

source_name: Fővárosi Vízművek Zrt. – beszerzési tervek és közbeszerzési közzétételek
why_relevant: Template case for utility buyers (víz-, táv- és hulladékszolgáltatók) that procure customer-payment channels, cash-desk POS and account services; publishes multi-year procurement plans and procedure disclosures.

source_name: Semmelweis Egyetem Beszerzési Igazgatóság (+ ÁKB állandó közbeszerzési bizottság)
why_relevant: Largest Hungarian medical university/clinic group; centralised procurement directorate publishing közbeszerzési dokumentumok. Representative pattern for university and hospital buyers of cash-desk POS, patient-payment and account services.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár – decentralizált önkormányzati számlavezetés (Treasury account service)
why_relevant: Structural demand-killer/shifter: since Oct 2025 the Treasury provides decentralised account-keeping for municipalities and their budgetary organs, free on both bank and treasury sides, with mandatory sweeping of balances above 5% of prior-year expenditure. This directly shrinks the commercial-bank municipal account market that this cell tracks — essential context for interpreting notice volumes.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – 194/2025. (VII. 8.) Korm. rendelet az önkormányzati számlavezetés részletszabályairól
why_relevant: The legal instrument governing whether and how a municipality may keep a commercial-bank account at all. Any amendment resets the addressable market and the tender pipeline for municipal account services; also useful for defining exactly which bodies remain free to tender.

source_name: EFER – Központi Elektronikus Fizetési és Elszámolási Rendszer (SZEÜSZ, operated by IdomSoft; KIFÜ connection projects)
why_relevant: Central state e-payment rail (POS at counters, VPOS card-not-present, bank transfer) that public bodies — including ASP-connected municipalities — join instead of contracting acquiring individually. Determines whether a municipality's card acceptance is a tender opportunity or a central connection project; KIFÜ runs the connection-support procurements.

source_name: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) – önkormányzati jelentések
why_relevant: Audit reports on municipal financial and asset management routinely describe account-keeping arrangements, bank selection procedures and procurement compliance failures — revealing incumbent banks and contract irregularities that notices alone do not show.
